papers.abstract: To avoid the failure of clinical surgery due to "stress shielding" and the loosening of an implant, a new type of alloy, Ti-24Nb-4Zr-8Sn (TNZS), with a low Young's modulus acted as a new implant material in this work. Meanwhile, the surface characteristics, MC3T3-E1 cell behavior and in vivo osseointegration of the titanium and TNZS before and after sandblasting and acid etching were studied comparatively. TNZS and Ti had the same microstructure based on the transmission electron microscopy results. Meanwhile, the TNZS alloy had a lower Young's modulus and surface nanohardness compared with pure titanium. However, the corrosion resistance of Ti was better than that of the TNZS sample in simulated body fluid solution. In addition, the TNZS alloy after sandblasting and acid etching (SLATNZS) had excellent cell adhesion, proliferation, differentiation, ALP activity and in vivo osseointegration ability such as there being almost no soft tissue as compared with other implants. Based on the current results, the new type of Ti-24Nb-4Zr-8Sn alloy showed good potential and promising application prospects in its biochemical aspects.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了新型低弹性模量合金的生物学性能，但未涉及股骨柄应力遮挡或微动的力学分析。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not quantify proximal femur stress shielding in Gruen zones, report micromotion with contact modeling, or compare intact vs implanted femur biomechanics; it is a biological and material characterization study.

summary_zh.motivation: 为避免应力遮挡和植入物松动，开发低弹性模量合金。
summary_zh.method: 对比研究Ti和TNZS合金的表面特性、细胞行为及体内骨整合。
summary_zh.result: TNZS合金具有较低弹性模量，且经喷砂酸蚀后细胞黏附和骨整合能力优异。
summary_zh.validation: 通过体外细胞实验和体内动物植入验证生物相容性。

summary_en.motivation: To prevent implant loosening due to stress shielding, a new low-Young's-modulus alloy Ti-24Nb-4Zr-8Sn (TNZS) was investigated as an alternative implant material.
summary_en.method: Surface characterization, MC3T3-E1 cell behavior assays, and in vivo osseointegration studies were performed on titanium and TNZS before and after sandblasting and acid etching.
summary_en.result: TNZS exhibited a lower Young's modulus and nanohardness than pure titanium, and sandblasted/acid-etched TNZS showed superior cell adhesion, proliferation, differentiation, and in vivo osseointegration with minimal soft tissue formation.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell experiments and in vivo animal implantation with histology confirmed the biocompatibility and osseointegration potential of the new alloy.
